title: Prelude Hashstore ledger for multi-request KV isolation and reuse
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: repeated leading prompt segments (preludes) across unrelated requests waste GPU KV capacity and block optimal slab packing during continuous batching windows. Current prefix dedupe picks up exact token-level matches but misses semantically identical preambles that differ by whitespace, minor templating, or tokenization-induced boundary splits. Goals: (1) increase cross-request KV reuse for the first 32-256 tokens to lower aggregate per-token compute and memory; (2) reduce GPU slab fragmentation and peak resident memory; (3) preserve tenant isolation and correctness for multi-tenant pools. Proposal: implement a Prelude Hashstore ledger — a content-addressed index combining normalized prelude canonicalization, a stable locality-preserving hash, and compact bloom signatures to allow probabilistic match-with-validation. The ledger will record immutable KV fragment snapshots (fingerprint -> [sha256 fragment, shard_id, slab_offset, token_length, codec_meta]) using copy-on-write shadow pointers for multi-tenant isolation. A lightweight match path runs in the runtime fast path: canonicalize -> ld-hash -> consult bloom -> try dedupe claim (atomic refcount attempt) -> validation decode on hit. On miss, fall back to existing path. To avoid validation cost on every hit, we keep a short validation TTL (e.g., 1m) and tag hits as "trusted" for that epoch. Memory optimizations include packing prelude fragments into 4KB-aligned slab segments, opportunistic GPU memcpy coalescing for adjacent fragments, and an epoch-based compaction that reclaims small fragments by rewriting coalesced snapshots during low-load windows. Rollout plan includes feature-flagged experiments, canary on low-traffic tenants, telemetry for reuse-hit-rate and worst-case validation latencies, and automatic fallback to non-dedup flow if validation errors exceed threshold.

updates: 2026-02-11: Spike completed — built a prototype canonicalizer that normalizes whitespace, template slots, and UUID-like tokens. Early offline dedupe analysis over 10M preludes shows ~41% byte-level dedupe potential.

2026-02-18: Design review with runtime and security. Decision: use content-addressed sha256 for immutable fragment identity and small 64-bit locality hash for fast routing. Security asked for KMS-protected audit logs when fragments are shared across tenant pools; noted for follow-up infra task.

2026-02-23: Benchmarks on p4d.24 show validation decode adds ~120us median when done on GPU; introduced trusted-TTL to amortize cost. Memory compaction prototype reduces resident memory by ~6% on heavy-mix workloads when coalescing 4K-aligned fragments.

2026-02-28: PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4021) with core hashstore APIs and feature flag. Seeking design + infra review. Blocking: slab allocator API needs small extension to reserve compact-aligned ranges.
2026-03-03: UX/PM asked for per-customer opt-out for sharing within Dedicated pools. Added opt-out label and will add config surface in Dedicated control-plane by next cycle.

2026-03-05: Running canary across 3 tenants in staging — observed reuse-hit-rate 28% and overall token cost reduction 5.8% (below target). Next: increase canonicalization aggressiveness and iterate bloom parameters; infra to provision minimal audit logging storage for cross-tenant fragments.

notes_on_tradeoffs: Aggressive canonicalization increases reuse but risks over-merging distinct prompts (e.g., 'User: John' vs 'User: Jo'). We chose conservative slot masking for names/UUIDs and will iterate with an opt-in aggressive mode. Probabilistic bloom reduces lookup cost but introduces false positives that must be validated; we use a short trusted-TTL to reduce repeated validation. Copy-on-write shadowing maintains tenant isolation but adds bookkeeping overhead — mitigated by background compaction and epoch-based refcount reconciliation.
review_feedback: PM (Riley Gomez): Prefer explicit per-tenant sharing controls and clear cost/benefit dashboard before enabling on Dedicated tenants.
Security (Dana Li): Audit logs required for cross-tenant fragments; ensure logs are KMS-protected. Also requested threat model for fragment reuse attacks.
Design (Maya Singh): Offer a visual rollout indicator in Console's model dashboard showing reuse-hit-rate and per-route savings.
Runtime eng (Omar Reyes): Suggested adding an in-memory LRU of recent fragment validations to avoid repeated GPU decode on hot items.
